method: Per proposal, 2 reformulation TYPES: (A) has THIS recent technique been applied to THIS process? (B) has the PROCESS PROBLEM been solved with ANY ML (incl. simpler/older methods)? gap_real = NOT(A) AND NOT(B). A gap closed by a SIMPLER existing method still counts as closed -- 'recent technique' is no opportunity if a cheaper method already solves the application (anti-overselling).
KEY_FINDING: 2 of 5 recent-technique pairings are REJECTED because the application is ALREADY solved by a SIMPLER method: retting endpoint by 4-wavelength colour sensors + PCA/PLS-DA (2025-2026), and indigo-vat state by real-time RGB machine-vision colour tracking (2024). The recent/fancier technique is OUTCLASSED or PREEMPTED. The 3 survivors enable a capability NO existing method provides (not a fancier version of a solved task).

reformulations: (A) hyperspectral foundation model / HSI imaging ML applied to flax retting endpoint / degree-of-retting
(B) flax retting endpoint detection by ANY ML / sensor / spectroscopy / non-destructive monitoring

type_A_recent_technique_applied.evidence: No HSI-foundation-model paper specifically on retting endpoint. SpectralEarth/HyperFree/HyperspectralMAE are remote-sensing FMs; flax HSI work is on flaxSEED quality, not retting.

type_B_problem_solved_any_ml.evidence: ACTIVE 2025-2026 prior art on the SAME application: 'Development of a smart farming tool to monitor the degree of dew retting of flax stems' (Nature Sci Reports 2025, s41598-025-12801-1); 'Tracking flax dew retting by infrared vibrational spectroscopy + multivariate statistical analysis' (2025, S0926669025003449); 'Spectral colour changes... smart flax dew retting monitoring' (2026, S0168169926000025) -- shows 4 wavelengths (480/490/600/610nm) + PCA/PLS-DA predict retting stage, drone-mountable colour sensor for 'optimal moment to end retting'.

proposals.decision: REJECT -- application is already being solved (2025-2026), and by a SIMPLER, cheaper method (4-wavelength colour sensor) that outclasses a hyperspectral foundation model. Recent != better here.

reasoning_trace.inputs_seen: two reformulation searches (A technique-specific, B problem-general)
reasoning_trace.reasoning: Type A found nothing, but Type B found a CLUSTER of 2025-2026 work solving exactly 'detect the optimal retting endpoint via spectral/colour + ML'. The application gap is closed. Worse for the proposal: the published solution uses only 4 wavelengths + classical multivariate stats, which is cheaper and more deployable than an HSI foundation model -- so the recent technique is not just preempted, it is outclassed.
reasoning_trace.confidence: high -- multiple independent 2025-2026 sources on the exact application
reasoning_trace.could_be_wrong_if: the published colour-sensor method proves insufficient for some retting regimes where full hyperspectral SSL is genuinely needed (no current evidence of that)

reformulations: (A) Fourier/neural operator applied to charcoal kiln internal temperature-field reconstruction
(B) earth-kiln charcoal internal temperature field estimated by ANY ML from sparse thermocouples

type_A_recent_technique_applied.evidence: No FNO/neural-operator paper on charcoal kilns. Adjacent only: physics-informed neural operator for COMPOSITE curing (S026382232300541X), RecFNO (flow/heat fields).

type_B_problem_solved_any_ml.evidence: General sparse-sensor temp-field reconstruction exists ('Learning to Reconstruct Temperature Field from Sparse Observations', 2512.01196; POD/sparse 2502.13190) and rotary-kiln temp prediction via ML+CFD (S0032591024002912) -- but NONE applied to the traditional EARTH charcoal kiln. Rotary kiln != earth mound; general method != kiln deployment.

proposals.decision: CANDIDATE -- on-target earth-kiln internal-field reconstruction is unexploited; the technique is proven on ADJACENT thermal systems (feasible). Feasibility caveat: needs training data (simulated kiln physics or instrumented kilns).

reasoning_trace.reasoning: Both A and B found only ADJACENT work (composite curing, rotary kilns, generic field reconstruction), none on the traditional earth charcoal kiln. The on-target application -- reconstruct the buried mound's internal temperature field from a handful of thermocouples -- is genuinely unexploited, and the adjacency proves feasibility.
reasoning_trace.confidence: high on the gap; medium on field-deployability
reasoning_trace.could_be_wrong_if: a non-indexed forestry/biochar paper already did kiln field reconstruction, or generating training data for a buried mound proves impractical

reformulations: (A) time-series foundation model / zero-shot forecasting applied to indigo fermentation vat state/crash
(B) indigo vat health/state FORECAST (future) by any ML time-series method

type_A_recent_technique_applied.evidence: No TSFM/zero-shot-forecasting paper on indigo vats; the TSFM hits (Reverso/Mamba4Cast/TimeRAF) are generic.

type_B_problem_solved_any_ml.evidence: FORECASTING the vat's future trajectory/crash is unexploited. ADJACENT/related: real-time RGB machine-vision COLOUR tracking of indigo REDUCTION (Chiang 2024, J. Chinese Chem. Soc., jccs.202300386) -- but that is present-state MONITORING of reduction timing, NOT forecasting vat health; and general fermentation soft-sensors (industrial bio-fermentation, not the dye vat).

proposals.decision: CANDIDATE -- zero-shot FORECASTING of the vat sensor stream (predict a crash before it happens, no labeled per-vat history) is unexploited. DISCLOSE: present-state CV colour monitoring of indigo reduction EXISTS (2024); the gap is specifically future-state forecasting. Feasibility caveat: hardware-gated (probes must survive hot caustic vat) + rare-event (crash) forecasting is the genuine uncertainty.

reasoning_trace.inputs_seen: two reformulation searches + the indigo CV prior art surfaced in the visual search
reasoning_trace.reasoning: Forecasting (future-state) is distinct from the 2024 RGB colour-tracking (present-state reduction timing). No one forecasts the vat's trajectory with a TSFM. I DISCLOSE the 2024 CV monitoring so Gate 3 can weigh it -- it does not close the forecasting gap but it narrows the novelty claim and must be on the record.
reasoning_trace.confidence: medium-high -- forecasting gap is real, but feasibility is hardware/rare-event limited
reasoning_trace.could_be_wrong_if: a craftsperson would gain nothing from a forecast they cannot act on, or probes cannot survive the vat, making the forecast academic

reformulations: (A) vision-language / CLIP zero-shot anomaly detection applied to cork-oak bark stripping
(B) cork stripping cut-depth / cambium-damage detected by ANY computer vision / ML

type_A_recent_technique_applied.evidence: No CLIP/VLM anomaly-detection paper on cork. CLIP-AD/AnomalyCLIP/AF-CLIP are generic/industrial (MVTec).

type_B_problem_solved_any_ml.evidence: No cork-stripping cambium-damage CV/ML found; searches returned generic structural/crop damage detection, nothing on cork bark stripping or cambium exposure.

proposals.decision: CANDIDATE -- on-target zero-shot anomaly flagging of an about-to-split/cambium-exposing strip is unexploited. Feasibility caveat: cork bark is OUT-OF-DISTRIBUTION for CLIP (FADE's 89.6% is on MVTec objects); and there is no labeled set even to VALIDATE it -- so it is a pilot, not a drop-in.

reasoning_trace.reasoning: Neither the technique-specific nor the problem-general search found any cork-stripping CV. The gap is real. But the same no-labeled-data property that makes zero-shot attractive ALSO means there is no way to validate the detector without field data -- an honest pilot-stage caveat.
reasoning_trace.confidence: medium -- gap real, but OOD transfer + unvalidatable without field data
reasoning_trace.could_be_wrong_if: experts already judge cut depth reliably by eye/feel (the proposal's own caveat) so an unproven OOD detector adds no value; or cork CV exists in non-indexed industry practice

reformulations: (A) vision-language / CLIP zero-shot anomaly detection applied to indigo vat surface/flower state
(B) indigo vat surface state read by ANY computer vision / machine vision

type_B_problem_solved_any_ml.evidence: ON-TARGET prior art: 'Color analysis and tracking of the reduction of an indigo solution in real-time using LabVIEW and machine vision' (Chiang & Lin 2024, J. Chinese Chem. Soc. jccs.202300386 / SSRN 4525584) -- a digital camera + LabVIEW machine vision tracks RGB colour to determine optimal dyeing timing from the vat. The application 'use computer vision to read the indigo vat's state' is ALREADY DEMONSTRATED with a simpler method. NOTE: this is on-target prior art that PHASE-2 penetration (count 0) MISSED -- penetration correction flagged to crosscheck.

proposals.decision: REJECT -- the CV-reads-indigo-vat-state application already exists (2024, RGB machine vision). A VLM zero-shot detector is a fancier tool for a substantially solved application, not a NEW application. Recent != new here.

reasoning_trace.inputs_seen: two reformulation searches; the 2024 LabVIEW machine-vision indigo paper
reasoning_trace.reasoning: Type A (VLM-specific) found nothing, but Type B found a 2024 machine-vision system that reads the indigo vat by colour to time dyeing. The proposal's narrower anomaly/health framing overlaps heavily with this solved monitoring task, and the simpler RGB method likely extends to health monitoring. Honesty (R13): I will not count a fancier tool for an already-demonstrated application as an opportunity. This also corrects PHASE-2's indigo penetration from 0 to >=1.
reasoning_trace.confidence: high -- a concrete 2024 on-target CV paper exists
reasoning_trace.could_be_wrong_if: vat-DEATH anomaly detection is genuinely distinct from reduction-timing colour tracking and remains unexploited -- but the burden is on showing that, and the core CV-reads-vat application is taken

summary.penetration_correction: indigo_vat on-target should be >=1 (2024 LabVIEW machine-vision colour tracking), not 0 -- surfaced in PHASE 4, fed to crosscheck.
